discretion: A screenshot proves the walk ran, not that it shows the claim. The reviewer judges the visible claim and source mapping; rendered-state assertions grow row by row in the agent tests. No-feature-impact reasons are declarations for review, not proof.
unmapped_instruction: add a row or declare no feature impact (give a reason for each path)

FL-200.label: Spin up new palaces easily: one command creates a fresh palace with its own database, schema and token in the owner's project, reachable by name; the app can point at any palace the owner has; a test palace is where verification agents train and is dropped whole afterwards.
FL-200.walk: Run the new-palace command with a name; a fresh empty palace answers by that name; point the app at it, save a memory, then drop it whole; the owner's main palace is untouched throughout.

FL-208.label: The vault: one owner-only env file per workflow holds the keys its tools need; a value is never printed, logged, journaled or packed, and no agent can read it.
FL-208.walk: Pipe a value into `nocturne vault set <workflow> <NAME>`: it lands in vault/<workflow>.env (mode 600 in a 700 folder) and the command prints the name and the path only. Run the saved bundle, then search every transcript, journal, log, the packed archive, the Palace database and the captures for the value: none. Save a job that tells its agent to read the vault file with the read tool and with cat: both are refused and no card offers to open it.

FL-209.label: A tool runs with its keys and the agent never sees them: `nocturne tool run <name>` executes the bundle's own code with the vault's variables; in a saved job that is not a boundary crossing, and the walls a recipe declares are crossed unattended once the owner confirmed them at save.
FL-209.walk: In the bundle folder, `nocturne tool run <name> [args]` runs the tool with its key. Run the saved job: its thread carries one line per tool (the name and the --help first line), the agent runs the tool as one plain command, the service it calls accepts the key, and the thread shows the tool's output only. Save a recipe whose prompt needs curl and declares nothing: the run parks as waiting at its boundary card. Save the same recipe with allow ["remote"]: `nocturne jobs save` shows the wall and asks once (a no saves nothing); confirmed, the run completes with no card, and the Jobs module names what it crosses unattended.
